    Long-running sessions (~8 MB session files, 2+ days) crash with FatalProcessOutOfMemory from giant ConsString flattening/regex replacement inside flatMap. With five production crash reports, this is a high-severity stability signal despite being closed as no-action.

  7. #11527 — Bedrock: a new BedrockRuntimeClient is created for every request [OPEN]
    Each model call creates a fresh client, credential provider, and HTTP/2 session. With SSO profiles this can trigger a GetRoleCredentials round trip per request, adding latency and credential churn.

  8. #11529 — Tool order depends on registration order, so the same tools can bust the prompt cache [OPEN]
    getCurrentTools() returns insertion order, so tools that reconnect or load via tool_search move to the end of the map. This breaks prompt-cache stability and connects directly to the cost issues in #10024.

  9. #11567 — Typing slows down in long sessions: getSessionName() scans every entry on each render [CLOSED, bug, no-action]
    At ~400k entries, key-to-render p50 rises from 1.5 ms to 21 ms, with 94% of busy CPU in SessionManager.getSessionName(). The issue was closed no-action, but the profile is concrete and likely to recur.

  10. #11538 — google-generative-ai: streamed parts with separate thought signatures are merged or dropped [OPEN]
    The Google stream parser coalesces text/thinking parts and retains only the last thoughtSignature, losing replay fidelity for thinking continuity. Two comments, but provider-side correctness issues tend to affect multiple models.

Key PR Progress

  1. #11545 — Anthropic message threads [OPEN]
    Adds support for Anthropic’s server-side message threads: when a session ID is set and caching is on, Pi can send only new messages instead of the full history each turn. This could materially reduce token usage and cost.

  2. #11562 — Start new sessions in the cwd’s default directory [OPEN]
    Fixes session storage semantics when a session is opened with a cwd from another project. /new, /fork, and /clone now use the session’s cwd default folder instead of treating the old folder as a custom --session-dir.

  3. #11546 — Cap pi.exec output at 256 MiB [CLOSED]
    Bounds combined stdout/stderr via ExecOptions.maxBuffer, terminates oversized commands, and returns truncated/killed status. A practical safeguard against runaway memory use in agent-executed commands.

  4. #11577 — Pick the smaller of PNG and JPEG when resizing images [CLOSED]
    Fixes the resize path always preferring PNG when it fit under the byte limit, even when the JPEG was much smaller. Directly addresses #11550 and avoids unnecessary payload inflation.

  5. #11572 — Do not retry Zhipu usage-limit errors (code 1308) [CLOSED]
    Zhipu/Z.ai plan caps return HTTP 429 with code 1308; the generic 429 pattern previously made Pi retry futilely. The fix distinguishes a quota cap from transient rate limiting.

  6. #11565 — Stop writing OSC 133 prompt markers in regular mode [CLOSED]
    Prevents TUI messages from being interpreted as shell prompts by terminals that display OSC 7501 program status, such as Rex and newer iTerm2. Fixes disappearing “working” indicators.

  7. #11556 — Let the SDK stream resolve auth for summaries [CLOSED]
    Fixes compaction, branch summaries, and bug-report summaries in createAgentSession sessions by letting modelRuntime.streamSimple resolve stored OAuth credentials instead of passing an access token as apiKey.

  8. #11544 — Kill the daemon’s commands when it is terminated [CLOSED]
    Prevents orphaned commands when a local Unix daemon is closed: the daemon now handles SIGTERM so kill_all runs instead of dying before cleanup.

  9. #11543 — Strip private-parameter CSI sequences in stripAnsi [CLOSED]
    Fixes ANSI stripping for sequences with private prefix bytes (<, =, >), so SGR mouse reports and secondary device attributes no longer leak fragments like 35;59;1M into rendered text.

  10. #11571 — Warn when an npm package update leaves the installed version unchanged [CLOSED]
    Addresses a registry-cache mismatch between npm view and npm install <name>@latest during pi update --extensions, making a silent no-op update visible to the user.

Hot Discussions

Show and tell

  • #11503 — pi-rs: a Rust port of the headless core
    A community Rust port of Pi 0.74.2’s headless core (agent loop, seven built-in tools, session JSONL, CLI surface, system prompt), with behavioral parity verified “atom by atom.” The author also shares a DeepSeek API compatibility finding. One comment and 1 👍.

Q&A

  • #11574 — How to upload an npmjs package to Pi package source?
    A package author asks how to publish and share a Pi package with the community. The lack of an obvious answer highlights a documentation/discovery gap around third-party package distribution.

Feature Request Trends

  • Provider abstraction hardening: sanitize OpenAI-specific fields for compatible providers (#9508), preserve Google thought signatures (#11538), reuse Bedrock clients (#11527), and handle provider-specific auth metadata correctly.
  • Prompt-cache stability and cost accounting: stable system-prompt heads and tool ordering (#10024, #11529), Bedrock cache warming (#11528), OpenRouter session IDs (#10022), and authoritative OpenRouter cost/BYOK data (#8940).
  • Long-session reliability: OOM crashes (#11570), render-time scans (#11567), context-usage accounting (#11534), and token-estimation clamping (#10988).
  • MCP and tool discovery: namespace-scoped tool_search queries (#11558), robust WWW-Authenticate parsing (#11539), and deterministic tool ordering for cache stability.
  • Extension contracts and packaging: explicit session_start message-ordering rules (#11157), recoverable unsupported image formats (#11552), configurable OAuth/Copilot timeouts (#11549), and clearer package publishing guidance (#11574).
  • Terminal UX portability: Windows/Zellij wheel handling (#9656), Apple Terminal Shift+Enter behavior (#11559), RTL rendering (#11580), and cleaner OSC/CSI handling (#11565, #11543).

Developer Pain Points

  • Provider-specific 400/422 failures remain a recurring tax. OpenAI-compatible endpoints, OpenRouter context limits, Google thought signatures, Bedrock credentials, and Zhipu quota errors all require provider-aware handling rather than generic request paths.
  • Prompt-cache invalidation is costly and hard to see. Dynamic tool selection, registration-order changes, and system-prompt head movement can silently re-bill conversations; users are asking for deterministic ordering and better cost visibility.
  • Long sessions degrade or crash. Large session files trigger V8 OOMs, per-render scans, and context-accounting problems, making multi-day agent sessions risky.
  • Extensions can violate core assumptions. Injecting messages at session_start, using tools.-prefixed names with small local models, or emitting unsupported image formats can break transcripts or provider requests.
  • Terminal and multiplexer differences create inconsistent UX. Windows/Zellij, Apple Terminal, RTL text, and OSC/CSI sequences all produce platform-specific behavior that is difficult for users to diagnose.
  • Session storage and resumption semantics are confusing. Opening a session from another project can change where /new, /fork, and /clone save, and --session-dir detection has been mistaken for custom storage.
  • Community package distribution lacks a clear path. The npm package publishing question and the Gondolin packaging fix (#11582) both point to onboarding/documentation friction for extension authors.
Qwen Code — QwenLM/qwen-code

Qwen Code Community Digest — 2026-10-30

Source: github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code · Data window: updates through 2026-10-29

1. Today's Highlights

The CLI shipped v0.26.4, a light release whose only user-facing feature is host-theme inheritance for generated UI views; the matching TypeScript SDK v0.1.26 and Desktop v0.26.4 were published alongside it. Engineering velocity is concentrated almost entirely in CI and release reliability: of the 20 most-commented PRs, more than half are infrastructure hardening (macOS suite partitioning, Web Shell smoke isolation, runner routing, Maven cache correctness, release notifier reconciliation). The most substantive open discussion remains context immutability for self-hosted models (#14215), where low prompt-processing speed makes mutable context expensive.

2. Releases

Release Notes
v0.26.4 (release) Primary CLI release. No known breaking changes. Feature: feat(generated-ui): follow the host theme in generated views (#15798). Release body is a placeholder (_See the complete change list below._), so the changelog is effectively the PR list.
sdk-typescript-v0.1.26 Bundles CLI 0.26.4, built from the same branch/ref as the SDK. The release body still contains stale text referencing CLI 0.26.3, suggesting a template/automation artifact worth cleaning up.
desktop-v0.26.4 Includes fix(config): report controls that were silently dropped (#15794) by @yiliang114, plus managed-session documentation updates.
v0.26.3-nightly.20261028.ca204559a7 Nightly cut from release/v0.26.3-nightly.20261028.ca204559a7; carries the same fix(config) change and managed docs edits.

Takeaway: a coordinated CLI + SDK + Desktop release train at 0.26.4. The only net-new product capability is theme inheritance for generated views; everything else is carried forward from 0.26.3.

3. Hot Issues

Only 3 issues were updated in the 24h window, so all three are covered rather than a top-10 selection.

  1. #14724 — Main CI failed: Managed Agent gate, no test identified · OPEN · type/bug, autofix/skip · 84 comments A bot-filed main-branch CI failure that has now been open for 10 days with 84 comments and no 👍. The extreme comment count on an autofix/skip-labeled item signals an automation loop or repeated human triage rather than genuine community debate — the single highest-noise item in the tracker.

  2. #14215 — Context immutability for self-hosted models · OPEN · P2, feature-request, performance, memory, caching, context-performance, need-discussion · 7 comments, 1 👍 The most substantive community request in the window. The reporter argues that features like memories, dreams, suggestions, and sessions all assume fast prompt processing; on self-hosted hardware with slow prefill, mutable context becomes prohibitively expensive. Requested behavior is an immutable context mode that preserves prefix-cache hits. Labeled need-discussion, so maintainer input is the blocker.

  3. #15251 — Fleet Shepherd Dashboard · OPEN · 0 comments Auto-maintained operational dashboard for the repo's agent fleet. Its current state is notable: the tick reports 2 autofix runs wedged in queued (oldest 2026-10-...), with syncs: 0 · dispatches: 0 · releases: 0. This is effectively a public health signal that the autofix pipeline is stalled.

4. Key PR Progress

  1. #15871 — refactor(managed-agent): split server into Maven modules (@doudouOUC) Decomposes the Managed Agent Server into six production Maven modules plus one unpublished verification module, with framework-neutral contracts defining boundaries between control-plane orchestration, Runtime Broker orchestration, persistence, and adapters. The largest architectural change in flight.

  2. #15870 — refactor(managed): remove persisted public message snapshots (@doudouOUC) Removes persisted public message snapshots from the managed server — a data-model simplification that likely reduces storage growth and snapshot/strea m divergence.

  3. #11854 — feat: add hybrid code mode (@DragonnZhang) Long-running (since 2026-09-14) feature adding a Codex-aligned tools.mode enum: direct, code_mode, code_mode_only. In code_mode, ordinary tools stay directly callable while also exposing an isolated exec JavaScript tool with nested JS declarations. The most significant capability addition under review.

  4. #15887 — feat(serve): enable remote access from settings without restarting (@yiliang114) Adds Settings → Connections → Allow remote connections to a running qwen serve. Remote access defaults off; a local operator can enable it live, then copy the address and a separate bearer token into another Web Shell's connection form. Meaningful UX win for daemon workflows.

  5. #15634 — feat(channels): deliver injected messages into the running turn (@Eric-GoodBoy-Tech) Adds a fourth channel dispatchMode, inject: messages arriving mid-turn go to the running turn's mid-turn queue and are read at the next tool-batch boundary instead of being buffered until turn end. Directly addresses agent responsiveness in channel sessions.

  6. #15888 — fix(ci): partition the complete macOS test suite into bounded jobs (@yiliang114) Splits macOS CI into seven jobs (three CLI shards, two core shards, remaining workspace suites, standalone/runtime scripts) with the original check retained as an aggregate gate. Stacked on #15884/#15883. A direct response to macOS suite timeouts.

  7. #15886 + #15884 — Web Shell smoke isolation (@yiliang114) #15886 pins browser smoke to ubuntu-latest for every admitted run, decoupled from the shared Linux runner fleet; #15884 moves Chromium profiles and shared-memory temp files onto the runner temp directory. Together these target the recurring smoke failure tracked in #15060.

  8. #15885 — fix(ci): route the E2E build job through the pool-first runner expression (@yiliang114) Aligns the E2E shared build job with the repo-wide routing convention: prefer self-hosted ecs-qwen when enabled, fall back to hosted Ubuntu, plus the standard self-hosted disk setup. Closes a routing inconsistency.

  9. #15854 — perf(release): reuse verified native audio prebuilds across releases (@yiliang114) Reuses native audio prebuilds from a successful official main release when build inputs match; validated cache hits skip the entire native build matrix, with any lookup/download/validation failure falling back to rebuilding all five targets. A clear release-latency win.

  10. #15829 — fix(vscode): keep sibling model settings when writing provider config (@2SinceJuly) Fixes a real data-loss bug: configuring a Coding Plan or provider from the VS Code companion rewrote settings.model with only name, silently deleting sibling keys. Now writes name and its paired baseUrl key-by-key. High user impact relative to its small diff.

Also worth watching: #15852 (release notifiers file issues only on real failures and reconcile stale ones), #15730 (job token for publish checkout), #15274 / #15286 (Maven cache/result-preservation hardening, both autofix/needs-human), #15771 (Actions queue census on the Fleet Shepherd dashboard), #11486 (qwen update --target-version).

5. Hot Discussions

Omitted — no Discussion data was provided in this dataset.

6. Feature Request Trends

  • Context and cache economics for self-hosted deployments. #14215 is the clearest signal: prefix-cache preservation, context immutability, and lower prefill cost. The roadmap/context-performance + scope/memory + scope/caching label cluster indicates this is a recognized roadmap axis, not a one-off.
  • Tool-invocation architecture. #11854 (tools.mode: direct / code_mode / code_mode_only) points toward a Codex-aligned model where tools are callable both directly and from an isolated JS exec sandbox.
  • Live/remote serving ergonomics. #15887 seeks zero-restart remote access with token-based auth for qwen serve — the daemon is being treated as a first-class deployment target.
  • Mid-turn message injection. #15634 requests interruptible, tool-boundary-aware message delivery in channel sessions instead of end-of-turn buffering.
  • Deterministic, offline-capable installation. #11486 (--target-version without npm discovery) reflects demand for pinned, reproducible standalone installs, including custom QWEN_UPDATE_BASE_URL mirrors.
  • Editor integration fidelity. #15829 shows VS Code companion config writes must be non-destructive to sibling settings — a "don't lose my config" class of request.

7. Developer Pain Points

  1. CI instability is the dominant tax. At least 8 of the top 20 PRs are CI fixes. Recurring themes: shared runner network contention (#15886), Chromium temp/shared-memory behavior in Web Shell smoke (#15884), macOS suite duration (#15888), inconsistent runner routing (#15885), and Maven cache write-back failure modes (#15274, #15286). Contributors are spending review bandwidth on test infrastructure rather than product code.
  2. Autofix automation is stalling, not helping. Issue #15251 reports 2 autofix runs wedged in queued; #14724 has accumulated 84 comments on a main-CI failure; two autofix/needs-human PRs (#15274, #15286) have sat open since 2026-10-22. The bot produces volume, but a growing share requires human rescue.
  3. Release automation false positives. #15852 documents that both fan-out release notifiers treat cancelled runs as failures and file issues, and that neither can close those issues when a later attempt ships. Combined with the placeholder v0.26.4 notes and the stale "0.26.3" text inside the 0.1.26 SDK release body, release metadata is drifting from reality.
  4. Silent config mutations destroy user state. Two independent tickets in one window — Desktop's fix(config): report controls that were silently dropped (#15794) and VS Code's settings.model overwrite (#15829) — indicate a systemic pattern: writers replace config objects rather than merging keys.
  5. Self-hosted users feel like second-class citizens. #14215 articulates the frustration directly: cutting-edge features (memories, dreams, suggestions, sessions) are designed around fast hosted prompt processing and degrade badly on slower self-hosted hardware.
  6. Opaque or missing release notes. v0.26.4's changelog ships as _See the complete change list below._, forcing users to reconstruct changes from the PR list.

Digest generated from GitHub metadata only. Issue/PR bodies were truncated in the source data; comment counts were unavailable for PRs and are reported as-is for issues.

item.content:encoded:
OpenClaw 生态日报 2026-10-30

Issues: 170 | PRs: 500 | 覆盖项目: 5 个 | 生成时间: 2026-10-29 18:48 UTC

  • OpenClaw
  • Hermes Agent
  • IronClaw
  • QwenPaw
  • ZeroClaw

OpenClaw 项目深度报告

OpenClaw 项目摘要 — 2026-10-30

数据窗口： 过去 24 小时，截至 2026-10-29。
数据说明： Issue 为按评论数排序的前 50 个；PR 为前 30 个样本。提供的数据中没有 PR 评论数，因此 PR 排名基于提供的排序和标签。

1. 今日概览

OpenClaw 正处于发布与分诊的极高活跃阶段：过去 24 小时有 170 个 Issue 和 500 个 PR 得到更新，其中 131 个活跃 Issue 和 291 个开放 PR，同时还有一个补丁版本发布。新版本 v2026.10.9 是安全与依赖加固补丁，而不是功能版本。Issue 队列主要由核心可靠性主题主导——会话状态生命周期、崩溃/唤醒恢复、记忆提升、消息丢失和提供商认证——而不是外观类请求。项目正在快速交付安全修复，但多个 P0/P1 可靠性 Issue 仍未关闭且没有关联修复 PR，因此整体健康度可概括为 高速推进但可靠性风险升高。

2. 发布

v2026.10.9 — 安全/依赖补丁

发布说明重点介绍了正在修补的运行时依赖漏洞：

  • MCP schema 校验： fast-uri 4.2.3 会拒绝格式错误的 URI scheme 和 host。
  • 输入边界： 过大的 Zod 集合会在 A2UI 和 Discord 嵌入式应用 SDK 中被提前拒绝。
  • IMAP 发件人解析： 迁移到 nodemailer 10.1.4，加强伪造发件人处理。

破坏性变更： 发布说明未提及。
迁移说明： 未提及。这似乎是一个可直接替换的补丁版本。
建议： 由于该版本明确以安全为重点，建议升级。

一个发布流程信号：Issue #187490 跟踪 2026.10.9 验证期间观察到的 flaky 测试。发布将其归类为 flaky，但政策要求在 main 上并行修复。

3. 项目进展

数据集报告过去 24 小时有 209 个已合并/已关闭 PR 更新。可见样本只识别出一个已关闭 PR：

  • PR #187819 — CLOSED：“fix: prevent shared-state hangs after service installation drift.” 这解决了服务安装策略变更或被复制时共享状态 worker 准入挂起的问题，包括 Linux 上运行中的系统 Gateway 可能选中一个无关的陈旧用户服务安装的情况。

多个开放 PR 显示在重要领域有活跃工作：

  • 模型目录 / thinking profiles： PR #187730、PR #187754、PR #187716 — 堆叠工作，使目录行拥有 thinking profiles，并改进 Kimi、DeepSeek、Mistral 和 Moonshot 模型的推理重放。
  • Discord / Codex 持久化： PR #177691 — 修复 Gateway 重启后 /codex detach 和 /codex bind 丢失的问题。它带有 P1、兼容性和安全边界合并风险标签，并且仍需要证据。
  • 记忆索引韧性： PR #187539 修复通过同主机 OpenAI 兼容嵌入服务器时 memory_search 超时的问题；PR #187797 处理嵌入批处理上限被截断的错误。
  • Codex 恢复： PR #187776 在后台清理稳定后恢复 Codex 会话。
  • Agent/会话正确性： PR #180214 在压缩期间保留活动请求来源；PR #180247 保留工具超时结果；PR #182553 和 PR #187833 处理排队消息上下文与溢出摘要；PR #187527 修复子代理完成后父仪表板发布的问题。
  • 安全/沙箱： PR #187825 修复远程 shell 沙箱路径裁剪问题，该问题可能将 " x.txt" 解析为 x.txt。
  • UI/CLI 打磨： PR #187831 在原生状态检查期间保留已保存的选择；PR #187522 处理 stdin 读取时的环境取消；PR #187830 将工作区冲突恢复保持在聊天启动之外；PR #187823 允许操作员关闭只读 Gateway 横幅。

4. 社区热门话题

最活跃的 Issue

主题 条目 信号
记忆召回 / 提升 #150635 — 22 条评论 短期召回保留会每晚驱逐已召回条目，因此“dreaming deep phase”永远不会提升。
记忆提升不一致 #164923 — 19 条评论 一个工作区提升 0/512 个候选，而兄弟工作区提升 50–90%。
崩溃恢复 / 会话状态 #166634 — 18 条评论 延迟回收检查点失败会导致 Agent 在崩溃恢复后永久不可用。
原生主机执行 / 共享状态 #177656 — 17 条评论 2026.10.5 上至少有 28 次失败，伴随共享状态完整性准入错误且没有子结果。
状态生命周期租约争用 #159094 — 14 条评论 Gateway 拥有租约，但内部 worker 报告另一个进程拥有状态生命周期。
控制 UI WebChat 抖动 #164394 — 13 条评论 滚动长记录时出现连续的微小上下颤动。
唤醒恢复运行时失败 #158592 — 11 条评论 主机睡眠/唤醒后，一个 Agent 的模型运行时发布超时，并且直到重启才恢复。

最活跃的 PR 主题

PR 评论数不可用，但提供的头部 PR 样本主要由以下内容主导：

  • Discord/Codex 状态持久性： PR #177691，P1，存在兼容性和安全边界风险。
  • 模型目录重构： PR #187730、PR #187754、PR #187716。
  • 记忆索引可靠性： PR #187539、PR #187797。
  • 会话/Agent 正确性与 UX： PR #180214、PR #180247、PR #187527、PR #187831。

底层需求： 用户正在将 OpenClaw 作为持久化、多通道、多 Agent 运行时来运行。社区参与度最高的问题不是功能愿望清单项；它们是对可预测的记忆提升、持久会话状态、可恢复的 Gateway 进程，以及当运行时所有权或提供商认证失效时更清晰诊断的诉求。

5. Bug 与稳定性

以下严重性标签来自 Issue 元数据。许多条目并非在过去 24 小时内首次报告，但在该窗口内有活动并得到更新。

P0 / 发布阻断类

  • Issue #166634 — P0：延迟回收提交检查点失败会导致 Agent 在崩溃恢复后不可用。Agent 会以 UNAVAILABLE 永久拒绝 chat.history、chat.metadata、models.list 和进度卡片请求。未看到关联修复 PR。
  • Issue #158592 — P0：在 macOS 主机睡眠/唤醒后，准备好的模型运行时发布对一个 Agent 超时；在 Gateway 重启前，每条入站消息都以“runtime owner was not published”失败。未看到关联修复 PR。
  • Issue #160762 — P0：claude-cli + Telegram 会丢弃在一轮对话中途发送的消息；被排空的提示携带上一条消息的正文。造成消息/数据丢失影响。未看到关联修复 PR。
  • Issue #161341 — P0：Codex 认证导入在 Windows 上总是失败，报“The Codex credential reader could not stop”，即使原生 Codex 登录有效。未看到关联修复 PR。

P1 / 高影响稳定性

  • Issue #177656 — P1：原生主机执行返回共享状态完整性准入错误，且没有子结果；在稳定版 2026.10.5 上至少有 28 次失败。未看到关联修复 PR。
  • Issue #159094 — P1：Gateway 拥有状态生命周期租约，但内部 worker 报告另一个 OpenClaw 进程拥有它，从而关闭数据库执行准入。未看到关联修复 PR。
  • Issue #155396 — P1：普通 Codex 工具轮次可能在最终答案恢复期间因 provenance_rejected 而故障关闭，丢失实质性最终答案。未看到关联修复 PR。
  • Issue #187579 — P1：Pi500 重启会因重新复制已安装插件依赖而产生约 1.5 GB 的不必要写入，并过早报告就绪。未看到关联修复 PR。
  • Issue #187099 — P1：在恢复切换通道上，排队回复从未被回收；诊断以 keep_lane/active_reply_work 拒绝，导致仪表板主会话不可用。未看到关联修复 PR。

安全 / 数据完整性

  • Issue #173058 — 安全，P2：tools.fs.workspaceOnly 未限制文件工具，因为 Agent 运行时还将 OpenClaw 状态根作为允许的工作目录接收。未看到关联修复 PR。
  • Issue #155457 — P2：Anthropic 工具调用在大型编辑时偶尔因格式错误的流式 JSON 参数失败。未看到关联修复 PR。
  • Issue #187588 — P2：针对现有本地 PDF 的 Telegram MEDIA: 行从未被派发；文本到达，但不发送文档，也不记录错误。未看到关联修复 PR。

稳定性 / 运维质量

  • Issue #187490 — P2：2026.10.9 发布验证中出现的 flaky 测试；跟踪在 main 上并行修复。
  • Issue #164690 — P2：claude-cli 运行会为每个 stdio MCP 服务器启动两次；relay/anchor 包装器每个 stdio 子进程消耗约 144 MB，且不可配置。
  • Issue #185092 — P2：Windows 节点已配对，但浏览器控制因监听器所有权/认证错误失败。

评估： 多个 P0 Issue 自 9 月底或 10 月初以来一直开放，且仍缺少可见的关联修复 PR。这是主要的项目健康度担忧。相邻领域有有用的修复 PR——共享状态挂起、状态检查、记忆索引、沙箱路径处理和 Codex 恢复——但它们尚未覆盖最高严重性的会话状态和唤醒恢复故障。

6. 功能请求与路线图信号

  • 长生命周期会话： Issue #154482 请求为永久 MAIN 会话历史提供受支持的生命周期——按范围导出/裁剪或滚动——因为以连续性为重点的部署无法限制 transcript_events。相关：Issue #112638 关于 session.maintenance 未能限制存储。
  • 团队/多 Agent 组织： Issue #153686 请求在团队模式下保留每个 Agent 下的命名会话组，而不是扁平化为 pinned/recent。相关的路由隔离问题出现在 Issue #126533 和 Issue #154739。
  • 无障碍与 UI 打磨： Issue #154524 请求将聊天消息暴露为标题以便屏幕阅读器导航；Issue #167415 报告侧边栏行在悬停状态间展开/打开与一键 Archive 交换位置，存在误归档风险。
  • 技能学习 / 评估： Issue #150250 提出一种 Skill Workshop 能力，用于验证普通工作中的学习覆盖率和行为复用。
  • 运维 UX： PR #187823 为只读 Gateway 横幅添加关闭按钮；Issue #167316 报告 Android 反复为未知 Agent "openclaw" 查询 chat.history。

对下一版本的预测： 最强的近期信号是安全/依赖补丁、模型目录和 thinking profile 工作、记忆索引韧性，以及有针对性的状态/UI 修复。更广泛的架构请求——永久 MAIN 会话生命周期、团队模式命名组，以及深度的会话状态租约重设计——除非维护者将其优先作为发布阻断项，否则不太可能在下一个补丁中落地。

7. 用户反馈摘要

  • 用户依赖连续性。 长生命周期 MAIN 会话、记忆提升和记录保留是反复出现的关切。当短期召回上限或提升过滤器行为异常时，用户会失去持久个人 Agent 的核心价值（#150635、#164923、#154482）。
  • 多 Agent Gateway 是生产工作负载。 用户报告租约争用、跨会话信封、多 Agent 扇出和工作区特定的提升失败。他们需要隔离和清晰的所有权语义，而不仅仅是配置选项（#159094、#126533、#154739）。
  • 通道可靠性很重要。 Telegram、Discord、Matrix 和 Tlon 的 Issue 涵盖消息丢失、媒体未送达、提及门控、引用边界和重启后绑定丢失。这些是生产集成 Bug，而不是边缘场景功能请求（#160762、#187588、#164065、PR #177691、PR #187778）。
  • CLI 支持的提供商路径仍然脆弱。 Codex 和 claude-cli 的 Issue 涉及认证导入、OAuth 刷新锁、来源拒绝、格式错误的流式参数、重复 MCP 服务器和模型目录不匹配。用户希望重试、清晰的原因码和平台一致性（#161341、#156442、#155396、#155457、#164690）。
  • 满意信号： 安全补丁活跃，社区参与度高，维护者正在跨模型目录、记忆索引和 UI 进行合并/重构。不满意信号： 多个 P0 已开放数周，许多高价值 Issue 带有 stale 或 needs-product-decision 标签，发布验证仍会遇到 flaky 测试。

8. 积压关注

长期未响应 / 高影响 Issue

  • Issue #112638 — 创建于 2026-07-22，P2，stale。session.maintenance enforce 模式未限制存储，因为 thread/channel 条目豁免回收。长期数据增长风险。
  • Issue #126533 — 创建于 2026-08-20，P2，stale。当默认 bot 账户和更具体的绑定同时匹配时，多 Agent 扇出会丢弃或错误路由 MESSAGE_CREATE。消息丢失风险。

需要维护者关注的 PR

  • PR #177691 — P1，兼容性和安全边界风险，仍为“needs proof”。重要的 Discord/Codex 状态持久性修复。
  • PR #180200、PR #180214、PR #180247 — 创建于 2026-10-22，标记为可供维护者查看；涵盖 GitHub 重连流程、压缩来源和工具超时结果。
  • PR #182553 — 创建于 2026-10-24，P1，需要证据。排队消息运行时上下文标记；更窄的后续拆分到 PR #187833。
  • PR #187542 — dependabot actions-group 更新，等待维护者。低风险维护，但会增加审查队列负载。

结论： OpenClaw 高度活跃且对安全响应迅速，在模型目录、记忆索引和 UI 正确性方面有强劲的持续工作。主要风险是未解决的 P0/P1 会话状态、Gateway 恢复和消息投递故障集中出现，其中多个已开放数周且没有关联修复 PR。

横向生态对比

跨项目对比报告 —— 个人 AI 助手 / Agent 开源生态

日期： 2026-10-30
项目： OpenClaw、Hermes Agent、IronClaw、QwenPaw、ZeroClaw
数据说明： 各摘要使用的采样窗口以及评论/反应数据的可得性不同。下文的健康评分为分析师定性评分（0–10），并非直接基准测试。IronClaw 在本窗口内无活动。

1. 生态概览

个人 AI 助手 / Agent 开源生态正处于高活跃度但高度关注可靠性的阶段。各项目已不再主要围绕功能新颖性竞争；它们正趋同于持久化多通道运行、会话状态持久化、记忆正确性、提供商/认证韧性以及运行安全。OpenClaw 按吞吐量是规模最大、最活跃的参考点，而 Hermes Agent、QwenPaw 和 ZeroClaw 则占据更窄但技术上各具特色的细分领域。发布节奏并不均衡：只有 OpenClaw 交付了一个补丁，其他项目则在积累修复，等待后续版本切出。生态的主要风险并非贡献量，而是合并/评审能力以及尚未解决的高严重度可靠性欠账。

2. 活跃度对比

项目 Issues（近 24 小时） PRs（近 24 小时） 发布状态 健康评分
OpenClaw 170 个更新；131 个活跃/开放 500 个更新；291 个开放；209 个已合并/关闭 v2026.10.9 安全/依赖补丁；无破坏性变更 7.2/10 —— 迭代速度快、安全响应及时，但 P0/P1 可靠性风险偏高
Hermes Agent 17 个更新；17 个开放；0 个关闭 50 个更新；37 个开放；13 个已合并/关闭 无发布；发布前稳定期低迷 6.4/10 —— 吞吐量强，但发布停滞且积压增长
IronClaw 0 0 无 不适用 —— 本窗口内休眠
QwenPaw 13 个更新；9 个关闭 41 个更新；27 个开放；14 个已合并/关闭 无发布；正在稳定 2.3.0-beta.1 6.8/10 —— 活跃且响应及时，但 beta 版脆弱，且大型 PR 评审受限
ZeroClaw 1 个更新；1 个关闭；0 个活跃开放 50 个更新；49 个开放；1 个已合并/关闭 无发布；v0.9.0 前筹备中 5.5/10 —— 管线较深，但合并速度低，作者行动项积压

解读： OpenClaw 的 PR 更新量约为同类的 10×，并且是本窗口内唯一交付发布版本的项目。QwenPaw 在活跃同类中拥有最健康的合并比例，而 ZeroClaw 的评审瓶颈最为明显。

3. OpenClaw 的定位

相较同类的优势

  • 规模： 24 小时内 500 个 PR 更新、209 个已合并/关闭 PR、170 个 Issue 更新 —— 远高于 Hermes、QwenPaw 和 ZeroClaw。
  • 发布响应能力： 在其他项目未发布任何版本时，交付了一个安全/依赖补丁。
  • 广度： 覆盖多 Agent 网关运行、会话状态生命周期、记忆提升、模型目录/思考配置、Discord/Codex 持久化、记忆索引韧性、沙箱以及多种通道适配器。
  • 社区引力： 在此集合中拥有最大的可见贡献者和 Issue 管线；很可能成为持久化 Agent 运行时的实际参考实现。

技术路线差异 OpenClaw 是以网关为中心、运行时较重的架构。其 Issue 集中在状态生命周期租约、崩溃/唤醒恢复、记忆提升、消息丢失防护以及提供商认证上——也就是持久化多 Agent 运行时最艰难的操作核心。相比之下：

  • Hermes 更偏向桌面端/消息能力对齐以及安装/更新。
  • QwenPaw 更偏向控制台/插件/PawApp。
  • ZeroClaw 更偏向系统层面，围绕事件溯源持久化、Goal Mode 和 ZeroCode TUI。
  • IronClaw 在本窗口内不活跃。

社区规模对比 OpenClaw 的活跃度比同类高一个数量级：PR 更新为 500，而 Hermes/QwenPaw/ZeroClaw 为 41–50；Issue 更新为 170，而后者为 1–17。然而，OpenClaw 也集中了最多未解决的 P0/P1 可靠性 Issue，因此规模并不等同于全面更优的健康度。

4. 共同技术重点领域

记忆正确性与可信度 OpenClaw、QwenPaw、ZeroClaw 提升/召回淘汰、静默记忆丢失、并发存储安全、召回泄漏、检查点语义、可见遥测
静默失败可观测性 Hermes、QwenPaw、ZeroClaw、OpenClaw 原因码、可见警告、更新回执、超时反馈、仅调试级可见的失败、“success=True”掩盖数据丢失

共同信号： 用户正把这些系统当作生产基础设施，而不是演示项目。最高价值的工作越来越集中在可预测的状态、可观测的失败和安全自动化上，而非新的 UI 界面。

5. 差异化分析

项目 功能重点 目标用户 架构信号

6. 社区动能与成熟度

第一梯队 —— 规模领先者，快速迭代 + 持续交付

  • OpenClaw： 活跃度极高，贡献者基础庞大，已交付安全补丁。按规模看成熟度高，但由于未解决的 P0/P1 会话状态与恢复故障，可靠性风险也最高。

第二梯队 —— 快速迭代者，正在稳定

  • Hermes Agent： PR 吞吐量和贡献者多样性较强，但 Issue 关闭数为零且无发布。积压压力以及安装/更新回归是主要拖累。
  • QwenPaw： 合并速度快，分诊响应及时，但存在 2.3.0-beta.1 回归和大型 PR 评审瓶颈。首次贡献者信号良好。
  • ZeroClaw： 管线深、路线图阶段划分清晰，但 1 个合并对 49 个开放 PR。评审吞吐量和作者跟进是瓶颈；处于 v0.9.0 前。

第三梯队 —— 休眠

  • IronClaw： 报告窗口内无活动。

动能解读： OpenClaw 正以生态领先的规模迭代并交付。QwenPaw 相对其体量迭代最快。Hermes 在积累修复但未发布。ZeroClaw 有架构雄心，但受合并能力制约。

7. 趋势信号

  1. 持久、可回放的状态正在成为基本要求。
    OpenClaw 的会话状态故障、ZeroClaw 的仅追加事件历史、Hermes 的迁移/会话恢复缺陷，以及 QwenPaw 的回退/决策持久化需求，都指向同一项要求：Agent 必须能在崩溃、重启、迁移和压缩后继续存活，且不丢失工作。

  2. 记忆是信任面，而不是功能勾选项。
    静默记忆丢失、提升不一致、召回泄漏和并发写入数据丢失在 OpenClaw、QwenPaw 和 ZeroClaw 中均有出现。开发者应把记忆视为事务性、可观测的子系统，并具备明确的成功/失败语义。

  3. 静默失败比显性失败更糟。
    Hermes 的 Slack 状态回归、QwenPaw 的“success=True”记忆丢失，以及 ZeroClaw 的 600s 静默等待，都表明用户对 bug 的容忍度高于不可见 bug。原因码、警告和遥测现在已成为产品需求。

  4. 多通道一致性是竞争基线。
    Telegram、Slack、Discord、Matrix 和 Web 控制台都需要一致的媒体处理、富消息、输入中/状态指示器，以及重启后持久的绑定。通道特定回归是生产阻塞项。

  5. 提供商抽象仍然脆弱。
    Codex/claude-cli 认证、OAuth 锁、OpenRouter 定价/密钥轮换、思考控制、本地模型发现和模型目录不匹配反复出现。稳健的提供商层需要重试、认证恢复、成本正确性和清晰诊断。

  6. 安全控制必须精准，而不是表演式。
    沙箱路径逃逸、密钥暴露、审批路由和提示注入误报在所有活跃项目中都有出现。过度拦截普通文本会带来满意度风险；拦截不足则是安全风险。开发者需要经过校准、决策可解释的护栏。

  7. 安装/更新/打包是 Agent 产品的一部分。
    PM 修复失败、部分克隆、PyInstaller 资源遗漏、插件加载失败，以及更新回执卡在“running”都不是次要问题——它们决定用户能否可靠地运行 Agent。

  8. 评审/设计能力是生态瓶颈。
    ZeroClaw 单日 49 个开放/1 个关闭 PR，以及 QwenPaw 的 XXXL PR 队列表明，贡献量可能超过维护者带宽。拥有清晰架构决策记录和更小可评审 PR 的项目，将更快把社区动能转化为已交付的可靠性。

对 AI agent 开发者的结论： 应围绕持久状态、可观测记忆、通道一致性、提供商韧性、精准安全以及可靠的安装/更新路径来构建。功能广度很重要，但在本窗口内，生态的稀缺资源是在持久化、多通道运行下的可信度。

P1 — 安装阻塞项

  • #143150 · Desktop 在 gateway.multiplex_profiles: true 迁移后无法恢复先前会话 → storage_unavailable。阻塞对历史聊天数据的访问。未见修复 PR。
  • #110374 / #112866 / #132594 · Slack 状态/输入指示器在 slack-sdk ≥ 3.44 上静默失效。功能上只是表面问题，但会影响每一轮 Slack 交互。相关开放 PR #145832 修复的是 Slack display_name 处理，并非此回归。

7. 用户反馈摘要

痛点，以用户自己的表述：

  • “Windows 上的仅前端安装” — 用户已经手动解决了分布式 agent 问题，希望 Desktop 不再假设自己与 agent 同机部署。这是工作流请求，不是 bug。
  • “静默损坏” / “静默消失” / “静默失败” — “静默”一词出现在全部三份 Slack 报告中。用户对故障的容忍度远高于对没有错误暴露面的故障；具体抱怨是协议失败只写入 debug 日志。
  • “任何依赖环境都无法提交” — 在受影响的文件系统上，P1 的 PM 故障被描述为绝对失败，而非间歇性失败。
  • “更新成功后，更新回执仍停留在 'running'” — 信任问题：日志说成功，状态却说中断。用户无法判断自己的安装是否可靠。

满意信号： 重复贡献者参与度高（Jpalmer95 提交了多个 PR，thisisnotajokee 在一天内提交了三份精确的安装-更新报告，附带版本哈希与耗时），且 bug 报告详细、可复现——这表明用户群体投入度高、技术能力强，而不是充满挫败感。

不满意信号： Slack 回归已持续至少三个版本（v0.21.5 → v0.21.6 → v0.22.5 时代），并产生了重复报告而非解决方案。#38519 请求自六月起开放，有 31 个赞，却无可见决策。两者都在累积善意负债。

底层需求分析：

  • Agent 循环控制是情绪最激烈的话题（9 条评论）。用户记录了系统介入前约 6 次重复的相同工具调用，浪费 token 和 API 预算。wontfix 的处置值得注意——它很可能表明一种设计立场（例如 6 次重复保护被视为“按预期工作”），而非敷衍了事。这可能会以“可配置/更早的循环中断”请求的形式再次出现。
  • 会话状态一致性（#8464）：用户在会话中途切换模型后，期望所有操作——包括 compaction——都遵循当前活动模型。根因是 active_model 解析读取的是 agent 级配置而非会话上下文。
  • 静默数据丢失（#8500）是信任风险最高的开放议题：success=True 的报告掩盖了记忆丢弃，正是这类 bug 会侵蚀用户对自主记忆功能的信心。

今日关闭的增强类 issue 涵盖 agent 控制和长会话 UX 面：

  • #6189 save_decision() API — 结构化决策持久化，以在上下文压缩后存活。强烈的框架级诉求（先有鸡还是先有蛋问题：agent 忘记决策然后无法归档它们）。
  • #4356 更细粒度的文件/工具守卫 — 只读路径、项目目录白名单，而非仅黑名单。
  • #4129 /rewind — 回滚文件/上下文以尝试替代提示或撤销 agent 造成的破坏（直接对标 Claude Code 的请求）。
  • #7740 Hub 模式管理员密码重置。
  • #8459 Web Console 中更便捷地访问未读推送消息。

对下个版本的预测： 鉴于 beta 回归负载，下一个即时版本很可能是 2.3.0-beta.2/GA 稳定化，而非功能交付。save_decision 式上下文持久性和 rewind 可能在 2.3.x 或 2.4 落地的信号：两者都针对与开放 bug #8500 相同的压缩丢失痛点类别，且项目已在投资相关记忆管道（#8457、#7835）。文件守卫粒度（#4356）与 #8492 中的 JEV/工具审查安全工作天然配对。

7. 用户反馈摘要

今日表达的痛点：

  • 成本/效率： 死循环（#6116）浪费的 token 和 API 调用——用户希望更早或可配置的循环中断。
  • 可预测性： 会话中途切换模型不被 /compact 遵循（#8464），打破了“你选什么就跑什么”的基本心智模型。
  • 对自主性的信任： 静默记忆丢失（#8500）和静默失效（#8488）比 loudly failure 更糟——用户反复要求可见的状态/警告。
  • 资源卫生： 仅仅访问设置页面就产生 690 MB RSS（#8490），在桌面/笔记本部署上很重要。
  • 运维基础： Hub 管理员仍无法重置用户密码（#7740）；密钥在 env list 中明文打印（已由 #8501 解决）。

满意度信号： 高质量、可复现的 bug 报告（尤其是来自 feng183043996，提交了 #6116、#6189、#8500 并撰写了 #8501）以及首次贡献者（#8291、#8400）表明社区参与度高。不满是beta 质量的摩擦，而非根本方向问题——若干抱怨是打包/生命周期回归而非架构性反对。

8. 待办关注

需要维护者带宽的大型 PR 和长期审查：

条目 时长 规模 关注点
#7874 feat(pawapp): redesign SDK and app control plane 自 2026-09-19（约 6 周） XXXL 架构分岔路口；阻塞下游 PawApp 工作。
#8034 fix(providers): bound inline media per request 自 2026-09-29（约 1 个月） XL 真实的网关故障缓解；仍处于 Under Review。
#7835 fix(memory): stop leaking auto-memory-recall payload to channels 自 2026-09-17（约 6 周） M 与 #8457 问题空间重复；需要合并决策。
#8231 fix(console): persist market install provenance 自 2026-10-13 M 阻塞第三方插件的可靠“全部更新”。
#8499 (WIP) feat(providers): extract local model management into plugin 新增 XXXL WIP；需在设计进一步膨胀前进行设计审查。

建议： 开放 PR 队列（27 个）偏向超大 diff——#7874、#8489、#8499、#8463、#8034。当前瓶颈是审查吞吐量，而非贡献量。两个记忆召回 PR（#7835、#8457）应协调为单一方向以避免冲突合并。开放 bug #8500（静默记忆丢失）目前无关联修复 PR，鉴于其信任影响应优先分诊。

数据窗口：2026-10-29 → 2026-10-30。来源：agentscope-ai/QwenPaw。

ZeroClaw — zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw

ZeroClaw 项目摘要 — 2026-10-30

仓库： github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw 数据窗口： 活动更新于 2026-10-29（过去 24 小时）

数据说明： 所提供数据集将所有条目的每 PR 评论数报告为 undefined，且 👍 = 0，因此无法计算“评论最多”/“反应最多”排名。下文各节按可观察信号（更新时间、标签权重、严重性、存续时间）排序，并在相关处加以标注。今天唯一已合并/关闭的 PR 不在所提供的 20 个条目中，因此无法点名。

1. 今日概览

ZeroClaw 今日呈现明显的评审受限、合并速度低态势：24 小时内共 51 次 issue/PR 更新，但仅有 1 个 PR 已合并/关闭，而 49 个仍开放——关闭与更新之比约为 1:50。Issue 队列基本清空（1 个更新，0 个仍开放/活跃），当日唯一关闭项是一个文档翻译清理 issue（#12076），并非代码变更。PR 构成偏重：前 20 个中有 11 个（55%）为 size:XL，3 个带有 risk:high；而 20 个中有 9 个（45%）处于 needs-author-action，这表明存在作者跟进积压，而不仅仅是维护者评审积压。没有发布版本，且在可见窗口内没有 PR 被标记为已合并——这与 v0.9.0 前后的预发布筹备期一致，该版本已作为 release 标签出现在关闭的 issue 上。贡献者集中度显著：20 个可见 PR 中有 8 个是来自单一作者（Audacity88）的 zerocode 范围工作，其中若干被标记为 distinguished contributor。

活动评估： 分诊/更新活动高，吞吐量低；流水线深度健康，合并延迟处于警告水平。

2. 发布

过去 24 小时没有新发布。 最新发布列表为空。

仅有前瞻信号：已关闭 issue #12076 带有标签 release:v0.9.0，同时描述的是对 v0.8.7 中引入的目录内容进行修复。这意味着 v0.9.0 是下一个计划版本，并且至少部分 v0.8.7 之后的文档修正正被并入其中，而不是进入 v0.8.x 补丁。该数据集未提供破坏性变更或迁移说明。

3. 项目进展

今日已合并/关闭： 1 个 PR（身份未出现在所提供的 top-20 切片中）+ 1 个 issue。

  • #12076 — 已关闭（docs，release:v0.9.0） — “发布由完整通读目录发现的 v0.8.7 翻译修复。”范围：docs/book/po 目录（fr、ja、es、zh-CN），大多数修正在 v0.8.7 新增页面，尤其是 plugin-release-acceptance.md。报告为信息不正确，1 条评论，提交后约 1 天内关闭（创建于 2026-10-28，更新于 2026-10-29）。仅文档条目，处理迅速。

可见的进行中功能推进（未合并）：

  • 目标执行生命周期 — #11881（Goal Mode V1，提案 4/12）已明确分阶段推进，正在等待运行时放置审批。
  • 仅追加的会话事件历史 — #11921，该集合中影响面最大的变更（risk:high、size:XL，数十个领域标签）。
  • 渠道对齐 — Telegram 富消息（#11862）以及 Telegram/Slack 的推理流式输出（#11744）继续推进 Matrix → Telegram/Slack 功能迁移。

小结：当日已完成的工作是文档维护；当日活跃的工作是一个大型、未合并的功能栈。

4. 社区热点

由于评论/反应数不可用，以下按更新时间 + 标签权重 + 范围列出信号最强的活跃讨论串。值得注意的是，全部 20 个可见 PR 都在 2026-10-29 更新，这看起来像一次批量分诊/标签清理，而不是各讨论串的自然讨论。

条目 为何重要
#11921 feat(session): append-only session event history 影响面最大的开放 PR（risk:high、size:XL，约 60 个领域标签）。重新定义规范会话/执行历史与重放语义——触及每个渠道、提供商和工具。
#11301 fix(agents): durable committed-rename recovery across CLI, gateway, RPC priority:p1、risk:high、size:XL，已开放 29 天。许多子系统依赖的跨领域持久性修复。
#11881 feat(goal): accounted Goal execution lifecycle [4/12] 编号式多 PR 设计系列——数据集中最清晰的路标产物。受阻于核心运行时放置审批。
#12004 fix(memory): markdown store() append-only priority:p1 数据完整性修复；规模小（size:M），但用户影响大。
#11744 / #11862 相邻渠道功能（推理流式输出 vs. 富消息），很可能需要在 Telegram/Slack 消息渲染上做共享设计决策。

底层需求： 热点集合聚为两类需求——(a) agent 状态的持久性/一致性（会话、重命名、记忆）以及 (b) 渠道 UX 对齐，使 Telegram/Slack 与 Matrix 一致。二者都是“让它在规模化时可信”的需求，而不是新增功能面。

5. 缺陷与稳定性

按严重性/影响排序。注意：这些都不是今天报告的；它们是今天更新过的开放修复。

严重性 条目 Issue 是否已有修复 PR？
P1 — 数据丢失 并发 MarkdownMemory::store() 写入执行读-改-重写，可能丢失更新 memory:backend 是 — #12004，priority:p1，needs-maintainer-review
P1 — 状态滞留 Agent 重命名在 workspace/memory/cron/ACP/session 状态之前提交配置；部分失败会使状态留在旧别名下，且 CLI 无法恢复 release-gate、domain:security 是 — #11301，priority:p1，已开放 29 天，needs-author-action
P1/P2 — 安全误报 提示防护将任何裸 ; 或 | 标记为命令注入 → 普通文本、表格和工具输出返回 Suspicious/Blocked security、runtime 是 — #12068，size:XS
P2 — 挂起/超时 已清除的 ask_user/poll 引导请求会让守护进程等待完整工具超时（ask_user 为 600 秒），且没有用户可见信号 zerocode 是 — #11624
P2 — 工具损坏 在 Android 上，canonicalize("/system/bin/sh") 在 SELinux 下失败并返回 EPERM，尽管 execve 可用 → 每次原生 shell 工具调用都失败 config 是 — #12080，size:S
P2 — 稳定性 一次失败的 MCP 恢复会永久毒化连接（RecoveryBarrier::poison() 没有清除路径；health_check() 仅探测传输层） tool:mcp 是 — #12061，size:S
P3 — 性能/成本 人格文件（AGENTS.md、SOUL.md 等）在提示重建时重新渲染 → 编辑会击穿提示缓存 agent、runtime 是 — #11698，size:XL

解读： 每个已识别缺陷都已经有开放的修复 PR。约束是评审/合并能力，而不是诊断。三个 size:XS/S 修复（#12068、#12080、#12061）是今天可用的成本最低的稳定性收益。

6. 功能请求与路线图信号

明确分阶段推进的路线图：

  • Goal Mode V1 — #11881 是 12 个提案中的第 4 个，即一个正式计划。其自述为“分阶段基础，而非启用或合并请求”，并以核心运行时放置审批为前置门槛。属于多季度工作。
  • 仅追加的会话事件历史 — #11921：重放可重建状态而不重复外部副作用。这是持久化恢复/撤销的架构前提。

进行中的面向用户请求：

  • 渠道丰富度与透明度： Telegram 富消息（标题/列表/引用/表格，通过 channels.telegram.<alias>.rich_messages 选择启用，默认 false）— #11862；Telegram/Slack 的推理流式输出对齐（stream_reasoning = off|status|full）— #11744。
  • 运维控制： cost.allow_override 已有文档，但此前未接入任何逻辑；#11589 允许运维人员覆盖已超出的成本限制，而无需重启守护进程。
  • ZeroCode UX 集群： 转录中的消息时间戳（#11622）、用每窗格会话上限替代硬编码的 8（#11731）、非取消式刷新（F5）（#11457）、会话列表跨重启持久化（#11727）、可搜索的键位绑定（#11505）。
  • 记忆： 可选启用的外部重排（#12036，由例外请求 PR #12037 引用）。

对 v0.9.0 的预测： 很可能发布小型、范围受控的修复——文档/翻译修正、命令注入误报修复、Android shell 路径修复、MCP 连接驱逐、webhook 长时间运行超时（#11931），并可能包括 Markdown 记忆仅追加修复。考虑到今日 0 次合并、risk:high 标签以及明确的审批门槛，XL 条目（Goal Mode、会话事件历史、渠道流式输出、提示缓存稳定性）不太可能进入该版本。

7. 用户反馈摘要

该数据集中没有直接的用户评论（评论数不可用；唯一 issue 有 1 条评论）。痛点只能从 PR/问题陈述中推断，而这些陈述异常明确：

  • 对持久化状态的信任是主导主题。用户遇到的是静默失败：并发下记忆写入丢失（#12004）、重命名后 CLI“无法恢复”（#11301）、每次启动都会忘记已打开会话的侧边栏（#11727）。
  • 静默等待是反复出现的不满点：已清除的引导请求会导致 600 秒挂起且无 UI 反馈（#11624）；没有转录时间戳就无法判断事件顺序或持续时间（#11622）。
  • 误报的安全控制降低日常使用体验——普通文本和工具输出因注入被拦截（#12068）。这是满意度风险：误触发的安全功能被报告为阻碍，而非保护。
  • 文档漂移是真实抱怨：v0.8.7 发布的翻译目录包含不正确信息，只有通过完整人工通读才发现（#12076）。这表明 i18n 发布流程缺少验证关卡。
  • 平台广度摩擦： Android 用户被完全阻断在 shell 工具之外（#12080 → #12080）。
  • 满意度信号： 无可量化信号（所有 👍 = 0）。没有证据表明用户对方向不满；有证据表明用户对可靠性边界情况不满。

8. 积压观察

存在停滞风险、需要维护者关注的条目：

存续时间（截至 2026-10-30） 条目 阻塞因素
29 天 #11301 — 持久化已提交重命名恢复 priority:p1 + needs-author-action + risk:high；价值最高但未推进的修复。
28 天 #11457 — 非取消式会话刷新 distinguished contributor，小型行为修复，没有可见评审者。
27 天 #11505 — 设置操作 + 键位绑定过滤器 needs-author-action
23 天 #11589 — 运维成本限制覆盖 有文档但未实现的配置；中等用户价值，XL 范围。
9 天 #11921 — 仅追加的会话事件历史 risk:high + size:XL；需要架构决策，而不仅仅是评审。
7 天 #12004 — 记忆仅追加 priority:p1、needs-maintainer-review；廉价修复，P1 影响。

给维护者的流程观察：

  1. 合并吞吐量是瓶颈。 49 个开放对 1 个关闭，且 45% 为 needs-author-action，这表明分诊惯例把 PR 停在作者身上，却没有清晰的重新进入路径。
  2. 两个 docs(runtime) 例外请求 PR——#12063（agent 自有状态退役，引用 #9745/#9647）和 #12037（外部记忆重排）——表明贡献者在寻求架构许可，而不是代码评审。这些是只有维护者才能解除阻塞的治理决策。
  3. ZeroCode 上的单一作者集中度（8/20 个 PR）是 bus-factor 风险；其中四个带有 needs-author-action，如果该贡献者带宽受限，问题可能加剧。
  4. 快速修复现已可用： #12068、#12080、#12061 为 size:XS/S——一次评审即可清理三个稳定性条目，并把合并速度从谷底拉起来。

item.content:encoded:
OpenClaw Ecosystem Digest 2026-10-30

Issues: 170 | PRs: 500 | Projects covered: 5 | Generated: 2026-10-29 18:48 UTC

  • OpenClaw
  • Hermes Agent
  • IronClaw
  • QwenPaw
  • ZeroClaw

OpenClaw Deep Dive

OpenClaw Project Digest — 2026-10-30

Data window: last 24 hours, through 2026-10-29.
Data caveat: Issues are the top 50 by comment count; PRs are the top 30 sample. PR comment counts are unavailable in the provided data, so PR ranking is based on the supplied ordering and labels.

1. Today's Overview

OpenClaw is in a very high-activity release-and-triage phase: 170 issues and 500 PRs were updated in 24 hours, with 131 active issues and 291 open PRs, alongside one patch release. The new release, v2026.10.9, is a security and dependency-hardening patch rather than a feature release. The issue queue is dominated by core reliability themes—session-state lifecycle, crash/wake recovery, memory promotion, message loss, and provider authentication—rather than cosmetic requests. The project is shipping security fixes quickly, but several P0/P1 reliability issues remain open without linked fix PRs, so overall health reads as high velocity with elevated reliability risk.

2. Releases

v2026.10.9 — security/dependency patch

Release notes highlight runtime dependency vulnerabilities being patched:

  • MCP schema validation: fast-uri 4.2.3 rejects malformed URI schemes and hosts.
  • Input bounds: oversized Zod collections are rejected early in A2UI and the Discord embedded app SDK.
  • IMAP sender parsing: moves to nodemailer 10.1.4, hardening spoofed-sender handling.

Breaking changes: none stated in the release notes.
Migration notes: none stated. This appears to be a drop-in patch release.
Recommendation: upgrade is advisable because the release is explicitly security-focused.

One release-process signal: Issue #187490 tracks flaky tests observed during 2026.10.9 validation. The release classified them as flakes, but policy requires parallel fixes on main.

3. Project Progress

The dataset reports 209 merged/closed PR updates in the last 24 hours. The visible sample only identifies one closed PR:

  • PR #187819 — CLOSED: “fix: prevent shared-state hangs after service installation drift.” This addresses shared-state worker admission hangs when service-installation policy changes or is copied, including a Linux case where a running system Gateway could select an unrelated stale user-service installation.

Several open PRs show active work on important areas:

  • Model catalog / thinking profiles: PR #187730, PR #187754, PR #187716 — stacked work to let catalog rows own thinking profiles and improve reasoning replay for Kimi, DeepSeek, Mistral, and Moonshot models.
  • Discord / Codex persistence: PR #177691 — fixes /codex detach and /codex bind being lost after Gateway restart. It carries P1, compatibility, and security-boundary merge-risk labels and still needs proof.
  • Memory indexing resilience: PR #187539 fixes memory_search timeouts through same-host OpenAI-compatible embedding servers; PR #187797 addresses truncated embedding batch-limit errors.
  • Codex recovery: PR #187776 resumes Codex conversations after background cleanup settles.
  • Agent/session correctness: PR #180214 preserves active request provenance during compaction; PR #180247 preserves tool timeout outcomes; PR #182553 and PR #187833 address queued-message context and overflow summaries; PR #187527 fixes parent dashboard publishing after subagent completion.
  • Security/sandboxing: PR #187825 fixes remote-shell sandbox path trimming that could resolve " x.txt" to x.txt.
  • UI/CLI polish: PR #187831 preserves saved selections during native status inspection; PR #187522 handles ambient cancellation on stdin reads; PR #187830 keeps workspace conflict recovery outside chat boot; PR #187823 lets operators dismiss the read-only Gateway banner.

4. Community Hot Topics

Most active issues

Topic Item Signal
Memory recall / promotion #150635 — 22 comments Short-term recall retention evicts recalled entries nightly, so the “dreaming deep phase” never promotes.
Memory promotion inconsistency #164923 — 19 comments One workspace promotes 0/512 candidates while sibling workspaces promote 50–90%.
Crash recovery / session state #166634 — 18 comments Late reclamation checkpoint failure leaves an agent permanently unavailable after crash recovery.
Native host exec / shared state #177656 — 17 comments At least 28 failures on 2026.10.5 with shared-state integrity-admission errors and no child result.
State-lifecycle lease contention #159094 — 14 comments Gateway owns the lease, but internal workers report another process owns state-lifecycle.
Control UI WebChat jitter #164394 — 13 comments Continuous micro up/down tremble when scrolling long transcripts.
Wake-recovery runtime failure #158592 — 11 comments After host sleep/wake, one agent’s model runtime publication times out and never recovers until restart.

Most active PR themes

PR comment counts are unavailable, but the supplied top PR sample is dominated by:

  • Discord/Codex state durability: PR #177691, P1 with compatibility and security-boundary risks.
  • Model catalog refactor: PR #187730, PR #187754, PR #187716.
  • Memory indexing reliability: PR #187539, PR #187797.
  • Session/agent correctness and UX: PR #180214, PR #180247, PR #187527, PR #187831.

Underlying need: users are running OpenClaw as a persistent, multi-channel, multi-agent runtime. The community’s highest-engagement issues are not feature wishlist items; they are requests for predictable memory promotion, durable session state, recoverable gateway processes, and clearer diagnostics when runtime ownership or provider auth breaks.

5. Bugs & Stability

Severity labels below come from the issue metadata. Many items were not first reported in the last 24 hours but were active and updated in the window.

P0 / release-blocking class

Prediction for the next version: the strongest near-term signals are security/dependency patches, model-catalog and thinking-profile work, memory-indexing resilience, and targeted status/UI fixes. Broader architectural requests—permanent MAIN session lifecycle, team-mode named groups, and deep session-state lease redesign—are less likely to land in the next patch unless maintainers prioritize them as release blockers.

7. User Feedback Summary

  • Users depend on continuity. Long-lived MAIN sessions, memory promotion, and transcript retention are recurring concerns. When short-term recall caps or promotion filters misbehave, users lose the core value of a persistent personal agent (#150635, #164923, #154482).
  • Multi-agent gateways are production workloads. Users report lease contention, cross-session envelopes, multi-agent fanout, and workspace-specific promotion failures. They need isolation and clear ownership semantics, not just configuration options (#159094, #126533, #154739).
  • Channel reliability matters. Telegram, Discord, Matrix, and Tlon issues cover dropped messages, undelivered media, mention gating, citation boundaries, and restart-lost bindings. These are production integration bugs, not edge-case feature requests (#160762, #187588, #164065, PR #177691, PR #187778).
  • CLI-backed provider paths remain fragile. Codex and claude-cli issues involve auth import, OAuth refresh locks, provenance rejection, malformed streamed arguments, duplicate MCP servers, and model catalog mismatch. Users want retries, clear reason codes, and platform parity (#161341, #156442, #155396, #155457, #164690).
  • Satisfaction signals: security patching is active, the community is highly engaged, and maintainers are merging/refactoring across model catalog, memory indexing, and UI. Dissatisfaction signals: multiple P0s remain open for weeks, many high-value issues carry stale or needs-product-decision labels, and release validation still encounters flaky tests.

Cross-Ecosystem Comparison

Cross-Project Comparison Report — Personal AI Assistant / Agent OSS Ecosystem

Date: 2026-10-30
Projects: OpenClaw, Hermes Agent, IronClaw, QwenPaw, ZeroClaw
Data caveat: Digests use different sampling windows and comment/reaction availability. Health scores below are qualitative analyst ratings (0–10), not direct benchmarks. IronClaw had no activity.

1. Ecosystem Overview

The personal AI assistant / agent OSS landscape is in a high-activity but reliability-heavy phase. Projects are no longer competing mainly on feature novelty; they are converging on persistent multi-channel operation, durable session state, memory correctness, provider/auth resilience, and operational safety. OpenClaw is the largest and most active reference point by throughput, while Hermes Agent, QwenPaw, and ZeroClaw occupy narrower but technically distinct niches. Release cadence is uneven: only OpenClaw shipped a patch, while peers are accumulating fixes toward future cuts. The dominant ecosystem risk is not contribution volume but merge/review capacity and unresolved high-severity reliability debt.

3. OpenClaw’s Position

Advantages vs peers

  • Scale: 500 PR updates, 209 merged/closed PRs, and 170 issue updates in 24h — far above Hermes, QwenPaw, and ZeroClaw.
  • Release responsiveness: shipped a security/dependency patch while peers shipped nothing.
  • Breadth: covers multi-agent gateway operation, session-state lifecycle, memory promotion, model catalog/thinking profiles, Discord/Codex persistence, memory-indexing resilience, sandboxing, and multiple channel adapters.
  • Community gravity: the largest visible contributor and issue pipeline in this set; likely the de facto reference implementation for persistent agent runtimes.

Technical approach differences OpenClaw is gateway-centric and runtime-heavy. Its issues cluster around state-lifecycle leases, crash/wake recovery, memory promotion, message-loss prevention, and provider authentication — i.e., the hard operational core of a persistent multi-agent runtime. By contrast:

  • Hermes is more Desktop/messaging-parity and install/update oriented.
  • QwenPaw is console/plugin/PawApp oriented.
  • ZeroClaw is systems-oriented around event-sourced durability, Goal Mode, and ZeroCode TUI.
  • IronClaw is inactive in this window.

Community size comparison OpenClaw’s activity is an order of magnitude larger than peers: 500 PR updates vs 41–50 for Hermes/QwenPaw/ZeroClaw, and 170 issue updates vs 1–17. However, OpenClaw also carries the highest concentration of unresolved P0/P1 reliability issues, so scale does not equal uniformly superior health.

6. Community Momentum & Maturity

Tier 1 — Scale leader, rapid + shipping

  • OpenClaw: Very high activity, large contributor base, security patch shipped. Maturity is high by scale, but reliability risk is also highest due to unresolved P0/P1 session-state and recovery failures.

Tier 2 — Fast iterators, stabilizing

  • Hermes Agent: Strong PR throughput and contributor diversity, but zero issue closures and no release. Backlog pressure and install/update regressions are the main drags.
  • QwenPaw: High merge velocity and responsive triage, but 2.3.0-beta.1 regressions and large-PR review bottleneck. Good first-time-contributor signals.
  • ZeroClaw: Deep pipeline and clear roadmap staging, but 1 merge vs 49 open PRs. Review throughput and author follow-up are the bottleneck; pre-v0.9.0.

Tier 3 — Dormant

  • IronClaw: No activity in the reporting window.

Momentum read: OpenClaw is iterating and shipping at ecosystem-leading scale. QwenPaw is iterating fastest relative to its size. Hermes is accumulating fixes without a release. ZeroClaw has architectural ambition but is merge-constrained.

7. Trend Signals

  1. Durable, replayable state is becoming table stakes.
    OpenClaw’s session-state failures, ZeroClaw’s append-only event history, Hermes’ migration/session-resume bugs, and QwenPaw’s rewind/decision-persistence asks all point to the same requirement: agents must survive crashes, restarts, migrations, and compaction without losing work.

  2. Memory is a trust surface, not a feature checkbox.
    Silent memory loss, promotion inconsistency, recall leakage, and concurrent-write data loss appear across OpenClaw, QwenPaw, and ZeroClaw. Developers should treat memory as a transactional, observable subsystem with explicit success/failure semantics.

  3. Silent failure is worse than loud failure.
    Hermes’ Slack status regression, QwenPaw’s “success=True” memory drop, and ZeroClaw’s 600s silent waits show users will tolerate bugs better than invisible bugs. Reason codes, warnings, and telemetry are now product requirements.

  4. Multi-channel parity is a competitive baseline.
    Telegram, Slack, Discord, Matrix, and web consoles all need consistent media handling, rich messages, typing/status, and restart-durable bindings. Channel-specific regressions are production blockers.

  5. Provider abstraction remains fragile.
    Codex/claude-cli auth, OAuth locks, OpenRouter pricing/key rotation, thinking controls, local model discovery, and model-catalog mismatches are recurring. A robust provider layer needs retries, auth recovery, cost correctness, and clear diagnostics.

  6. Security controls must be precise, not theatrical.
    Sandbox path escapes, secret exposure, approval routing, and prompt-injection false positives appear across all active projects. Over-blocking ordinary prose is a satisfaction risk; under-blocking is a safety risk. Developers need calibrated guardrails with explainable decisions.

  7. Install/update/packaging is part of the agent product.
    PM repair failures, partial clones, PyInstaller asset omissions, plugin-load failures, and update receipts stuck in “running” are not side issues — they determine whether users can operate agents reliably.

  8. Review/design capacity is the ecosystem bottleneck.
    ZeroClaw’s 49-open/1-closed PR day and QwenPaw’s XXXL PR queue show contribution volume can outpace maintainer bandwidth. Projects with clear architectural decision records and smaller reviewable PRs will convert community energy into shipped reliability faster.

Bottom line for AI agent developers: build for durable state, observable memory, channel parity, provider resilience, precise security, and reliable install/update paths. Feature breadth matters, but in this window the ecosystem’s scarce resource is trustworthiness under persistent, multi-channel operation.

1. Today's Overview

QwenPaw shows high-velocity maintenance activity: 13 issues and 41 PRs were updated in the last 24 hours, with 9 issues closed and 14 PRs merged/closed against 27 still open. No new release shipped, but the activity is heavily concentrated on stabilizing the 2.3.0-beta.1 line, which generated several regression reports (plugin loading, desktop packaging, optional-dependency memory use). The project also closed a long-running wontfix decision on agent doom loops (#6116) and landed security/CLI hardening (#8492, #8501). Overall health is active but beta-fragile: strong contributor throughput and responsive triage, offset by a growing queue of large (XL–XXXL) PRs awaiting review. First-time contributors (#8291, #8400) indicate a healthy on-ramp.

2. Releases

None in this cycle.

3. Project Progress

Five PRs moved to closed/merged in the visible window, spanning security, providers, console UX, and website infrastructure:

  • #8492 fix(security): prevent false-positive approvals for Code Mode in JEV mode — tightens the tool-review gate so Code Mode operations aren't auto-approved incorrectly; directly relevant to agent safety.
  • #8497 fix(plugins): tolerate import cache refresh failures during plugin loading — the fix for the 2.3.0-beta.1 startup failure (#8473); restores plugin entry-point loading.
  • #8358 fix(providers): honor thinking defaults and declared wire controls — resolves a Console/backend mismatch where thinking_enabled=off was not transmitted to OpenAI-compatible providers.
  • #5490 feat(console): navigable fullscreen image gallery for chat media — long-lived feature (opened June) finally closed; wraps tool-card images in a single Image.PreviewGroup for gallery navigation.
  • #8253 feat(website): add JSON-driven evaluation index — bilingual evaluation leaderboard with Pareto frontier and SDK history.

Additional in-flight work advancing: memory-recall hardening (#8457, #7835), CLI secret masking (#8501), and Ollama model discovery (#8309).

4. Community Hot Topics

Item Activity Link
#6116 Doom loop: agent repeats same tool call in one turn 9 comments, closed wontfix Issue
#8464 Manual /compact ignores session-level model switch 4 comments, closed Issue
#8500 Auto-Dream silently drops memory, checkpoints anyway 2 comments, open Issue
#8473 All backend plugins fail to load in 2.3.0-beta.1 2 comments, closed (fix: #8497) Issue

Analysis of underlying needs:

  • Agent loop control is the most emotionally charged topic (9 comments). The user documented ~6 repeated identical tool calls before the system intervened, wasting tokens and API budget. The wontfix resolution is notable — it likely signals a design stance (e.g., the 6-repetition guard is considered "working as intended") rather than dismissal. This may resurface as a request for configurable/earlier loop-breaking.
  • Session state consistency (#8464): users switching models mid-session expect all operations — including compaction — to honor the active model. The root cause is active_model resolution reading agent-level config instead of session context.
  • Silent data loss (#8500) is the highest-trust-risk open thread: a "success=True" report masking dropped memory is exactly the class of bug that erodes user confidence in autonomous memory features.

5. Bugs & Stability

Ranked by severity (all reported/updated 2026-10-29):

  1. CRITICAL — #8473 2.3.0-beta.1: all backend plugins fail to load at startup (12/12 plugins on reporter's host). Root cause: unguarded importlib.invalidate_caches() in module_isolation.py:220, same root cause as prior #8265, new call site. Fix exists: #8497 (closed).
  2. HIGH — #8488 Desktop/PyInstaller build omits visual_compression assets → FileNotFoundError: atlas-gray-native.ts; Visual Compact silently no-ops with no user-visible warning. Packaging regression in 2.3.0-beta.1. Open, no fix PR referenced.
  3. HIGH — #8500 Auto-Dream silently drops a full day of memory when the extract step can't parse the agent reply, yet still checkpoints the files so they are never retried. Reports success=True with no telemetry. Open, no fix PR referenced.
  4. MEDIUM — #8464 Manual /compact always uses agent-level active_model, failing with 400 when that model strictly validates compaction params. Closed.
  5. MEDIUM — #8490 Opening Voice Transcription settings imports whisper into the server process (~690 MB RSS, never released) just to check availability. Open.
  6. LOW — #8486 Tool-call <> icon clipped on left edge — container lacks horizontal padding. Cosmetic. Open.

Regression cluster: three of the four open bugs (#8488, #8490, #8486) are from 2.3.0-beta.1-era builds, suggesting the beta needs a focused stabilization pass before GA. A security-adjacent hardening PR, #8501 (mask env var values in env list/env set), also addresses plaintext secret exposure in the CLI.

6. Feature Requests & Roadmap Signals

Today's closed enhancement issues span the agent-control and long-session UX surface:

  • #6189 save_decision() API — structured decision persistence to survive context compaction. Strong framework-level ask (chicken-and-egg problem: agent forgets decisions then can't archive them).
  • #4356 Finer-grained file/tool guard — read-only paths, project-directory whitelists rather than blacklist-only.
  • #4129 /rewind — rollback files/context to try alternate prompts or undo agent damage (direct Claude Code parity request).
  • #7740 Hub-mode admin password reset.
  • #8459 Easier access to unread push messages in the web Console.

Prediction for next versions: Given the beta-regression load, the immediate next release is likely a 2.3.0-beta.2/GA stabilization rather than feature delivery. Signals that save_decision-style context durability and rewind could land in 2.3.x or 2.4: both address the same compaction-loss pain class as open bug #8500, and the project is already investing in related memory plumbing (#8457, #7835). File-guard granularity (#4356) is a natural pairing with the JEV/tool-review security work in #8492.

7. User Feedback Summary

Pain points expressed today:

  • Cost/efficiency: Wasted tokens and API calls from doom loops (#6116) — users want earlier or configurable loop-breaking.
  • Predictability: Mid-session model switches not honored by /compact (#8464) breaks a basic mental model of "what you select is what runs."
  • Trust in autonomy: Silent memory loss (#8500) and silent no-ops (#8488) are worse than loud failures — users repeatedly ask for visible status/warnings.
  • Resource hygiene: 690 MB RSS from a mere settings-page visit (#8490) matters on desktop/laptop deployments.
  • Operational basics: Hub admins still can't reset user passwords (#7740); secrets print in plaintext in env list (addressed by #8501).

Satisfaction signals: high-quality, reproducible bug reports (notably from feng183043996, who filed #6116, #6189, #8500 and authored #8501) and first-time contributors (#8291, #8400) show an engaged community. Dissatisfaction is beta-quality friction, not fundamental direction — several complaints are packaging/lifecycle regressions rather than architectural objections.

8. Backlog Watch

Large PRs and long-running reviews that need maintainer bandwidth:

Item Age Size Concern
#7874 feat(pawapp): redesign SDK and app control plane Since 2026-09-19 (~6 wks) XXXL Architectural fork in the road; blocks downstream PawApp work.
#8034 fix(providers): bound inline media per request Since 2026-09-29 (~1 mo) XL Real gateway-failure mitigation; still Under Review.
#7835 fix(memory): stop leaking auto-memory-recall payload to channels Since 2026-09-17 (~6 wks) M Duplicates problem space with #8457; needs consolidation decision.
#8231 fix(console): persist market install provenance Since 2026-10-13 M Blocks reliable "Update All" for third-party plugins.
#8499 (WIP) feat(providers): extract local model management into plugin New XXXL WIP; needs design review before it grows further.

Recommendation: The open-PR queue (27) is skewed toward very large diffs — #7874, #8489, #8499, #8463, #8034. Review throughput, not contribution volume, is the current bottleneck. Two memory-recall PRs (#7835, #8457) should be reconciled into a single direction to avoid conflicting merges. Open bug #8500 (silent memory loss) currently has no linked fix PR and deserves triage priority given its trust impact.

Data window: 2026-10-29 → 2026-10-30. Sources: agentscope-ai/QwenPaw.

ZeroClaw — zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw

ZeroClaw Project Digest — 2026-10-30

Repo: github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw Data window: activity updated 2026-10-29 (last 24h)

Data caveat: the supplied dataset reports per-PR comment counts as undefined and 👍 = 0 across all items, so "most commented" / "most reacted" rankings cannot be computed. Sections below rank by observable signal (update recency, label weight, severity, age) and this is flagged where relevant. The single merged/closed PR today is not among the 20 items provided, so it cannot be named.

1. Today's Overview

ZeroClaw shows a strongly review-bound, low-merge-velocity day: 51 total issue/PR updates in 24h, but only 1 PR merged/closed against 49 still open — roughly a 1:50 close-to-update ratio. The issue queue was effectively cleared (1 updated, 0 open/active remaining), and the day's only closure was a documentation-translation cleanup issue (#12076), not a code change. PR composition skews heavy: 11 of the top 20 (55%) are size:XL and 3 carry risk:high, while 9 of 20 (45%) sit under needs-author-action, pointing to an author-follow-up backlog rather than a maintainer-review backlog alone. No releases shipped, and no PR is labelled as merged in the visible window — consistent with a pre-release staging period around v0.9.0, which already appears as a release label on the closed issue. Contributor concentration is notable: 8 of the 20 visible PRs are zerocode-scoped work from a single author (Audacity88), several flagged distinguished contributor.

Activity assessment: high triage/update activity, low throughput; healthy pipeline depth, warning-level merge latency.

2. Releases

No new releases in the last 24h. Latest Releases list is empty.

Forward-looking signal only: the closed issue #12076 carries the label release:v0.9.0 while describing fixes for catalogue content introduced in v0.8.7. This implies v0.9.0 is the next planned cut and that at least some post-v0.8.7 documentation corrections are being rolled into it rather than a v0.8.x patch. No breaking-change or migration notes are available from this dataset.

3. Project Progress

Merged/closed today: 1 PR (identity not present in the provided top-20 slice) + 1 issue.

  • #12076 — CLOSED (docs, release:v0.9.0) — "Ship the v0.8.7 translation fixes found by a full read of the catalogues." Scope: docs/book/po catalogues (fr, ja, es, zh-CN), with most corrections on pages new in v0.8.7, especially plugin-release-acceptance.md. Reported as incorrect information, 1 comment, closed within ~1 day of filing (created 2026-10-28, updated 2026-10-29). Fast turnaround on a docs-only item.

Feature advancement visible in-flight (unmerged):

  • Goal execution lifecycle — #11881 (Goal Mode V1, proposal 4/12) is explicitly staged and awaiting runtime-placement approval.
  • Append-only session event history — #11921, the broadest-blast-radius change in the set (risk:high, size:XL, dozens of area labels).
  • Channel parity — Telegram rich messages (#11862) and reasoning streaming for Telegram/Slack (#11744) continue the Matrix → Telegram/Slack feature migration.

Net: the day's completed work was documentation hygiene; the day's active work is a large, unmerged feature stack.

4. Community Hot Topics

Because comment/reaction counts are unavailable, the following are the highest-signal active threads by recency + label weight + scope. Notably, all 20 visible PRs were updated on 2026-10-29, which looks like a bulk triage/label sweep rather than organic per-thread discussion.

Item Why it matters
#11921 feat(session): append-only session event history Highest-blast-radius PR open (risk:high, size:XL, ~60 area labels). Redefines the canonical conversation/execution history and replay semantics — touches every channel, provider and tool.
#11301 fix(agents): durable committed-rename recovery across CLI, gateway, RPC priority:p1, risk:high, size:XL, open 29 days. Cross-cutting durability fix that many subsystems depend on.
#11881 feat(goal): accounted Goal execution lifecycle [4/12] A numbered multi-PR design series — the clearest roadmap artefact in the dataset. Blocked on core runtime-placement approval.
#12004 fix(memory): markdown store() append-only priority:p1 data-integrity fix; small (size:M) but high user impact.
#11744 / #11862 Adjacent channel features (reasoning streaming vs. rich messages) that likely need a shared design decision on Telegram/Slack message rendering.

Underlying need: the hot set clusters into two demands — (a) durability/consistency of agent state (sessions, renames, memory) and (b) channel UX parity so Telegram/Slack match Matrix. Both are "make it trustworthy at scale" needs rather than new surface area.

5. Bugs & Stability

Ranked by severity/impact. Note: none of these were reported today; they are open fixes updated today.

Sev Item Issue Fix PR exists?
P1 — data loss Concurrent MarkdownMemory::store() writes do read-modify-rewrite and can drop updates memory:backend Yes — #12004, priority:p1, needs-maintainer-review
P1 — stranded state Agent rename commits config before workspace/memory/cron/ACP/session state; partial failure leaves state under old alias and CLI cannot resume release-gate, domain:security Yes — #11301, priority:p1, open 29d, needs-author-action
P1/P2 — security FP Prompt guard flags any bare ; or | as command injection → ordinary prose, tables and tool output return Suspicious/Blocked security, runtime Yes — #12068, size:XS
P2 — hang/timeout Cleared ask_user/poll elicitations leave the daemon waiting the full tool timeout (600s for ask_user) with no user-visible signal zerocode Yes — #11624
P2 — broken tooling On Android, canonicalize("/system/bin/sh") fails EPERM under SELinux though execve works → every native shell tool call fails config Yes — #12080, size:S
P2 — stability One failed MCP recovery permanently poisons a connection (RecoveryBarrier::poison() has no clear path; health_check() only probes the transport) tool:mcp Yes — #12061, size:S
P3 — perf/cost Personality files (AGENTS.md, SOUL.md, etc.) re-rendered on prompt rebuild → edits bust the prompt cache agent, runtime Yes — #11698, size:XL

Read: every identified bug already has an open fix PR. The constraint is review/merge capacity, not diagnosis. The three size:XS/S fixes (#12068, #12080, #12061) are the cheapest stability wins available today.

6. Feature Requests & Roadmap Signals

Explicitly staged roadmap:

  • Goal Mode V1 — #11881 is proposal 4 of 12, i.e. a formal programme. Self-described as "a staged foundation, not an enablement or merge request," gated on core runtime-placement approval. Multi-quarter work.
  • Append-only session event history — #11921: replay rebuilds state without repeating external effects. This is the architectural prerequisite for durable resume/undo.

User-facing requests in flight:

  • Channel richness & transparency: Telegram rich messages (headings/lists/quotes/tables, opt-in via channels.telegram.<alias>.rich_messages, default false) — #11862; reasoning streaming parity for Telegram/Slack (stream_reasoning = off|status|full) — #11744.
  • Operator control: cost.allow_override documented but previously wired to nothing; #11589 lets an operator override an exceeded cost limit instead of restarting the daemon.
  • ZeroCode UX cluster: message timestamps in transcript (#11622), per-pane session cap replacing a hard-coded 8 (#11731), non-cancelling refresh (F5) (#11457), session-list persistence across restarts (#11727), searchable keybindings (#11505).
  • Memory: opt-in external rerank (#12036, referenced by exception PR #12037).

Prediction for v0.9.0: likely to ship the small, contained fixes — docs/translation corrections, the command-injection false-positive fix, the Android shell path fix, MCP connection eviction, webhook long-running timeout (#11931), and possibly the Markdown memory append-only fix. The XL items (Goal Mode, session event history, channel streaming, prompt-cache stability) are unlikely to make it given 0 merges today, risk:high labels, and explicit approval gates.

7. User Feedback Summary

No direct user commentary is present in this dataset (comment counts unavailable; 1 comment on the sole issue). Pain points must be inferred from the PR/problem statements, which are unusually explicit:

  • Trust in persisted state is the dominant theme. Users hit silent failures: lost memory writes under concurrency (#12004), a CLI that "could not resume" after a rename (#11301), a sidebar that forgets open sessions each launch (#11727).
  • Silent waiting is a recurring irritant: cleared elicitations that leave a 600s hang with no UI feedback (#11624); no way to tell event ordering or durations without transcript timestamps (#11622).
  • False-positive safety controls degrade ordinary use — prose and tool output blocked as injection (#12068). This is a satisfaction risk: security features that misfire are reported as blocking, not protective.
  • Documentation drift is a real complaint: v0.8.7 shipped translation catalogues with incorrect information, found only by a full manual read (#12076). Suggests the i18n release process lacks a verification gate.
  • Platform breadth friction: Android users are fully blocked from shell tooling (#12080 → #12080).
  • Satisfaction signal: none quantifiable (all 👍 = 0). No evidence of dissatisfaction with direction; evidence of dissatisfaction with reliability edge cases.

8. Backlog Watch

Items at risk of stalling, needing maintainer attention:

Age (as of 2026-10-30) Item Blocking factor
29 days #11301 — durable committed-rename recovery priority:p1 + needs-author-action + risk:high; the highest-value fix that is not moving.
28 days #11457 — non-cancelling session refresh distinguished contributor, small behavioural fix, no visible reviewer.
27 days #11505 — settings actions + keybinding filter needs-author-action
23 days #11589 — operator cost-limit override Documented-but-unimplemented config; moderate user value, XL scope.
9 days #11921 — append-only session event history risk:high + size:XL; needs an architectural decision, not just review.
7 days #12004 — memory append-only priority:p1, needs-maintainer-review; cheap fix, P1 impact.

Process observations for maintainers:

  1. Merge throughput is the bottleneck. 49 open vs 1 closed with 45% needs-author-action suggests a triage convention that parks PRs on authors without a clear re-entry path.
  2. Two docs(runtime) exception-request PRs — #12063 (agent owned-state retirement, refs #9745/#9647) and #12037 (external memory rerank) — indicate contributors are seeking architectural permission, not code review. These are governance decisions that only maintainers can unblock.
  3. Single-author concentration on ZeroCode (8/20 PRs) is a bus-factor risk; four carry needs-author-action, which may compound if that contributor is bandwidth-limited.
  4. Fast fixes are available now: #12068, #12080, #12061 are size:XS/S — a single review pass could clear three stability items and lift merge velocity off the floor.
